newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -FTSE options busy ahead of July expiry.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -FTSE options busy ahead of July expiry.

text.p: The erratic behaviour of the stock market on Thursday brought brisk trading in FTSE index options, dealers said.
The larger deals were volatility trades but there were also a significant number of positions rolled forward ahead of the contract expiry on July 18.
One of the larger volatility deals was from a seller of 1,000 December 5125 calls at 75p who hedged this by buying December FTSE futures.
Further deals along these lines were made by the same trader as the market meandered along. The trades will make money if implied market volatility decreases.

As volatility in the August series began to ease during the day, another trader bought straddles in FTSE -- betting that volatility will rise -- and the position was hedged by buying September futures.
The options position initially consisted of buying 500 August 4725 puts and calls at a net debit of 209p. Further purchases made bringing the total number of puts and calls bought to 1,225.
At the close of business on the stock market, cash FTSE was up 5.4 at 4767.8 while September futures were up six points at 4779.
Over in stock options, the July series for a number of food retailers were busy, mainly as a result of profit-taking ahead of expiry.
The most active food retailers were Asda Group, Safeway and J Sainsbury whose July options expire on July 16.
Asda shares closed up 3-1/4p to 142-1/2p while Safeway gained 13p to 400p and Sainsbury added 20p to 419-1/2p.
